Sound.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures. v2: added code link. Audio samples ( https://dhy02.github.io/editvoice-demo/ ); code ( https://github.com/DHY02/EditVoice )

Sound.title: VocalCoachBench: Benchmarking Audio-Language Models on Expert Feedback for Singing
Sound.summary: Recent audio-language models are increasingly evaluated on recognizing, describing, and reasoning about audio, but expert-facing applications require a different capability: producing feedback that identifies problems and suggests corrective actions grounded in the input. We introduce VocalCoachBench, a benchmark for evaluating audio-language models on expert vocal coaching feedback for singing. VocalCoachBench contains 515 recordings annotated by 18 professional vocal trainers, yielding 1,056 expert submissions and 12,051 atomic coaching claims. It comprises a same-song subset for controlled comparison and a diverse-song subset for segment-grounded feedback across varied songs and recording conditions. To accommodate the open-ended nature of expert feedback, VocalCoachBench sep- arates deterministic structured targets from claim-based assessment of free-form diagnosis and corrective guidance. Human annotation analysis shows that expert agreement varies strongly with label granularity, motivating hierarchical structured metrics and claim-based evaluation of open-ended feedback. Experiments with 12 recent audio-language models reveal a consistent gap: while models can compare performances and identify broad issue domains in free-form feedback, Top-3 fine-grained issue-label identification remains below label-prior baselines and strict diagnosis alignment stays below 7%. To our knowledge, VocalCoachBench pro- vides the first public testbed for evaluating audio-grounded expert feedback for singing, moving audio-language evaluation beyond description toward analytic feedback.
Sound.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations & Datasets Track

Sound.title: SpectralBridge: Adding High-Frequency Capability to Large Audio-Language Models
Sound.summary: Large audio-language models (LALMs) have become highly capable on a wide range of tasks spanning speech, music, and environmental sound. However, many modern LALMs resample input audio to 16 kHz mono, making all frequencies above 8 kHz unobservable. We present SpectralBridge, a lightweight extension that gives such a model access to the 8-16 kHz band by joining low- and upper-band representations with time-aligned paired cross-frequency attention. Applied to Audio Flamingo Next, the method trains only a small adapter and rank-8 LoRA modules, while leaving the original audio encoder, audio projector, and base language model frozen. SpectralBridge improves both zero-shot transfer and downstream fine-tuning: it raises zero-shot balanced accuracy on the ESC-50 audio classification dataset from 75.5 to 90.5, and when fine-tuned on Insect-10, a 10-way insect species task we construct from InsectSet459 recordings, under the same budget as a LoRA fine-tuned baseline, it reaches 55.4 balanced accuracy against the baseline's 26.2. On a benchmark where the answer depends only on the 8-16 kHz band, it gains 30 mAP over the frozen model. Erasing the upper-band stream from the trained model removes these gains, showing that they come from the high-frequency signal itself rather than from extra tokens or the adapted prompt format.
Sound.comment: Accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Real-Time Multimodal Conversational AI (ReMuCAI), Paris. 13 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables

Sound.title: PitchIn: Natural-Language Vocal Coaching from Unstructured Community Feedback
Sound.summary: Effective vocal coaching connects performance issues with corrective advice, but recordings paired with expert diagnoses and advice are scarce. Online singing communities provide a potential source of supervision, but observations and advice are scattered across unstructured comments. We introduce PitchIn, audio-language models for natural-language vocal coaching, and the PeerCoach Dataset: 14,445 instruction examples covering Focused QA, Overall Feedback, and Recognition QA. We compare target combinations on Qwen2.5-Omni and train PitchIn on Focused QA and Overall Feedback using Qwen2.5-Omni and MOSS-Music. On VocalCoachBench, the proportion of requested diagnosis-correction pairs matching an expert issue with valid advice rises from 21.3% to 61.0% for Qwen2.5-Omni and from 31.4% to 51.2% for MOSS-Music. Direct training on source comments yields only 19.8% for Qwen2.5-Omni. For Qwen, Focused QA alone reaches 65.6%, but adding Overall Feedback improves alignment with expert reviews and human preference. Both models improve expert-review alignment over pretrained baselines and are significantly preferred for usefulness (92.0% and 67.3%, respectively). Demo examples are available at https://hayeonbang.github.io/PitchIn.

Sound.title: UA-Bench: Benchmarking Large Audio-Language Models on Underwater Acoustic Recognition
Sound.summary: Large audio-language models (LALMs) are fast becoming a general interface to sound, yet how far their broad pretraining carries into specialized domains remains largely open. Vessel monitoring, maritime safety, and ocean sensing all depend on recognizing underwater signals, but to our knowledge LALMs have not been systematically evaluated on them. Annotated recordings are costly to collect, and a faithful synthetic alternative has to bring together many interacting factors: the structure of detection pulses, communication waveforms, and ship-radiated noise, and the sound-speed profile, geometry, and multipath propagation through which each reaches the receiver. We address this by proposing \textbf{UA-Bench}, to our knowledge the first large-scale benchmark for evaluating LALMs on underwater acoustic signal recognition. It comprises 375,051 audio records that couple parameterized sources with modeled propagation, so that every record can be traced to the conditions that produced it. The records span these three signal families, and each carries a three-level label hierarchy (13 leaf classes), a templated multi-turn dialogue, and source and channel metadata. We evaluate on a balanced 2,600-record subset with a gated coarse-to-fine protocol that locates each error at source routing, fine-grained classification, or output format, and add a paired silent-audio control to test whether the waveform is actually used. Nine open LALMs, evaluated without task-specific adaptation, reach only 2.0\%--13.1\% leaf accuracy, against a random reference of 7.7\%. The waveform helps source routing far more than leaf recognition (for one model, +29.5 versus +2.3 points over silence), and just four models gain reliably at the leaf level, by at most 4.7 points. UA-Bench thus gives a reference point for these models, and its released training partition supports follow-up adaptation work.

Sound.title: What Makes Codec Tokens Effective for Target Speaker Extraction? A Semantic-Acoustic Disentanglement Perspective
Sound.summary: Target speaker extraction (TSE) aims to recover a target speaker's speech from a speech mixture using an enrollment utterance. Recent codec-based generative approaches formulate TSE as conditional speech token generation and achieve promising perceptual quality. However, most existing systems rely on unified codec tokens that entangle linguistic content, speaker characteristics, and acoustic details, forcing a single model to jointly handle target selection, content semantic, and acoustic reconstruction. In this paper, we investigate whether disentangled semantic-acoustic codec representations are better suited to TSE. We first show that simply replacing unified codec tokens with semantic-acoustic tokens is insufficient and can even degrade performance when both remain handled by a unified generative model. Motivated by this observation, we propose a task-aware discriminative-generative framework, where a discriminative branch extracts target-related semantic information, while a generative branch predicts coarse acoustic tokens and refines them under semantic guidance. This specialization separates what is said from how it sounds while coordinating both factors in a factorized codec space. Experiments on Libri2Mix show that our method reduces dWER from 0.388 to 0.118 compared with a unified-codec baseline, while maintaining competitive perceptual quality and speaker consistency. Ablation studies confirm that the gains arise from task-aware semantic-acoustic modeling rather than representation disentanglement alone.

Sound.title: Unsupervised Data Drift Monitoring for Deployed Deepfake Speech Detectors
Sound.summary: Deepfake speech detectors are typically evaluated as binary classifiers on fixed benchmarks, but deployed systems face evolving attacks, codecs, speakers, and recording conditions, with labels unavailable during operation. This makes it difficult to know when a detector operates in familiar conditions and can be relied on. We propose an unsupervised drift monitor that operates on the internal embeddings of a deployed detector. The monitor compares each input against bona fide and spoof references using regularized Mahalanobis distances. These distances define trusted, ambiguous, and novel regions of the detector embedding space, allowing unfamiliar inputs to be routed for review. We evaluate the monitor on four modern detectors on three datasets. The monitor raises alerts for dataset mismatches and substantially reduces the security-critical case of accepting deepfakes at the cost of reduced automatic coverage. The results also show that drift affects both classes: bona fide recordings can move away from the training reference, increasing alert rates even in in-domain settings. Our findings suggest that deployed deepfake speech detectors should be treated not only as a binary classification, but also as a reliability problem.
Sound.comment: Accepted at IEEE International Workshop on Information Forensics and Security (WIFS) 2026

Sound.title: Predicting Audio Popularity: A Comparative Study of Metadata and Acoustic Features Across Music and Sound Effects
Sound.summary: This study addresses the prediction of audio popularity on an online sharing platform by leveraging both metadata and acoustic feature representations. Two distinct categories of audio content are considered: music and sound effects. Popularity is formulated as a supervised classification task based on two target variables: the number of downloads and the average user rating. We conduct a comparative evaluation of multiple machine learning models, including Random Forest, XGBoost, and a Neural Network model. Experiments are performed across different feature sets, including metadata, platform-provided descriptors, and eGeMAPS acoustic features. Results indicate that metadata consistently provide the most informative representation for predicting popularity. Nevertheless, acoustic features alone achieve performance significantly above chance level, demonstrating that intrinsic properties of the audio signal contribute to popularity prediction.

Sound.title: StepAudio 3 Realtime Technical Report
Sound.summary: Realtime spoken interaction demands deep reasoning, prompt responses, and fluid turn-taking. We present StepAudio 3 Realtime, an audio-language foundation model organized around a continuous listen-converse-think-act loop. Deep Perception captures rich acoustic cues to interpret user intent, while Seamless Duplex models synchronized audio streams to handle pauses, backchannels, and interruptions naturally. Crucially, we resolve the tension between deep deliberation and latency via Think-While-Speaking, executing private reasoning in parallel with spoken delivery. In reasoning mode, StepAudio 3 reaches a 73.0 macro average on StepAudioChat. With Think-While-Speaking, it achieves dialogue and reasoning performance comparable to dedicated reasoning models while speaking in real time. Furthermore, an integrated Voice Agent handles asynchronous tool execution without disrupting the dialogue flow. StepAudio 3 Realtime achieves top-tier performance across key dimensions: an exceptional 90.6 on the MMSU benchmark, 98.9 Overall on the Artificial Analysis Full-Duplex Bench, and a 56.0% macro task-success rate on $τ$-Voice.

Sound.title: PRB-WM: Physics-Regularized Beta World Models for Predictive Link Adaptation on Real Time-Varying Underwater Acoustic Channels
Sound.summary: Adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) improves the spectral efficiency of underwater acoustic (UWA) links, but its feedback is inevitably stale: sound propagates slowly, and by the time channel state information (CSI) arrives, the fast time-varying multipath channel has moved on. Predictive link adaptation therefore needs more than a point forecast: it needs a distribution over each candidate action's consequences. We propose PRB-WM, a physics-regularized Beta world model for predictive per-subcarrier link adaptation on real time-varying UWA channels. A persistence-anchored stochastic latent-space dynamics model learns how the channel evolves; a counterfactual outcome head evaluates, for every candidate modulation and coding scheme (MCS), a Beta-binomial distribution of bit errors on shared imagined futures; and a chance-constrained receding-horizon model predictive controller maximizes expected spectral efficiency subject to a bounded probability of violating the bit error rate (BER) target. To the best of our knowledge, PRB-WM is the first world model for UWA communications. In closed-loop replay of six measured sea-trial links from the public UWA Channel Library against a 24-method pool spanning the full methodological spectrum, PRB-WM attains a mean goodput 87% above the strongest baseline, ranks first on all six time-varying links at the longest lookahead, and is the only method whose realized frame risk decreases systematically with lookahead, meeting the BER-violation contract where no baseline does. Ablations confirm that rollout sampling dispersion is essential to the chance constraint and that the physics anchor is necessary for trainability.
Sound.comment: Submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. 15 pages, 13 figures, 3 tables, 2 algorithms

Sound.title: LLM-HB: Language-Aware LLM-Guided Hotword Biasing for Code-Switching ASR
Sound.summary: Code-switching (CS) speech, characterized by language alternation within a single utterance, is prevalent in multilingual communities and poses challenges to automatic speech recognition (ASR) due to rapid language transitions. We propose LLM-HB, a language-aware large language model-guided hotword biasing framework for code-switching ASR (CS-ASR). The framework incorporates a mixture-of-experts (MoE) adaptor and an auxiliary language prediction head to better capture and differentiate multilingual representations, while hotwords are injected through LLM-based prompting. Experiments on the ASRU2019 code-switching challenge test set demonstrate that LLM-HB achieves a 20.30% relative reduction in mixed error rate (MER) over the baseline, reaching 5.85% MER under a 15-distractor hotword setting. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to integrate LLM-guided biasing into code-switching ASR. We further release the extracted ASRU2019 hotword list to support future research.

Sound.title: X2Streaming-ASR: wait when uncertain, emit when ready for streaming ASR
Sound.summary: Streaming automatic speech recognition (ASR) for real-time voice agents and full-duplex dialogue must provide accurate partial transcripts with low commit latency. Existing systems commonly use a fixed chunk size, look-ahead, or target delay, or encourage emissions near estimated acoustic boundaries. These approaches do not directly optimize how much additional context to use at each output position under a single-pass, hard-commit constraint. We propose X2Streaming-ASR, which decomposes streaming recognition into when to commit and what to commit. Its three-stage training procedure first establishes streaming recognition ability, then warm-starts the commit policy with automatically probed trajectories, and finally refines the policy using character-level, segment-assigned group-relative rewards for recognition accuracy and latency. Across ten Chinese and English test sets, X2Streaming-ASR attains the lowest mean commit latency relative to forced-aligned endpoints, 32--109ms on Chinese characters and 12--85ms on English words, while recognition accuracy remains comparable to existing systems.Code is available at https://github.com/X-Square-Robot/X2Streaming-ASR.

Sound.title: MPASCNet: Magnitude-Phase-Aware Adaptive Spectral Compression for Compressed Music Restoration
Sound.summary: Compressed music restoration aims to recover high-fidelity audio from lossy codecs such as MP3 by restoring missing spectral content and reducing coding artifacts. Recently, generative adversarial networks and band-split models have made progress in compressed music restoration. However, existing methods either operate without explicitly modeling phase or rely on predefined frequency partitions, which may limit restoration performance and the use of input-dependent frequency information. To address these issues, we propose MPASCNet, a Magnitude-Phase-Aware Adaptive Spectral Compression network. Instead of using fixed bands, MPASCNet combines magnitude and phase features to guide cross-attention, adaptively compressing full-resolution spectral features into compact tokens. These tokens are then processed by a spectro-temporal backbone to model spectral-temporal dependencies. Finally, separate decoder branches reconstruct the full-resolution magnitude and wrapped phase spectra. Experiments on MP3 restoration show that MPASCNet outperforms the Apollo and AEROMamba baselines across multiple restoration metrics while using only 6.49 M parameters. The code is available at https://github.com/xinghour/MPASCNet.

Sound.title: Behavior-Conditioned Animal Vocalization Generation: Event-Aware Modeling and Multidimensional Evaluation
Sound.summary: Behavior-conditioned animal vocalization generation aims to synthesize vocalizations from natural-language descriptions of animal behaviors, social interactions, and contexts. This task remains largely unexplored, with limited behavioral text supervision and substantial variation in vocalization duration. We construct the Behavior-Vocalization Dataset (BeVo) by integrating public bioacoustic data from six species with natural-language behavioral conditions derived from species-specific ethological and bioacoustic literature, totaling 31,191 events. We then adapt a rectified-flow-based generator with Event-Aware variable-length modeling, which encodes vocalizations at their actual durations and uses masks to prevent attention to padded latent positions and exclude these positions from the training loss. We evaluate vocalization discriminability, acoustic distribution fidelity, and language-aligned representation fidelity. Experiments show that task-specific adaptation improves all evaluated metrics compared with its zero-shot baseline, while Event-Aware modeling further increases vocalization-anchor macro accuracy from 59.86% to 61.99% and reduces Frechet Audio Distance from 1.40 to 1.22. Conditioning analyses further show that behavioral conditions improve target-anchor discriminability, while swapping behavior shifts generations toward the corresponding vocalization anchors. Demos are available on our project page.
Sound.comment: Submitted to ICASSP 2027. Project page: https://persimmontian.github.io/BCAVG

Sound.title: SyncReward: Human-Aligned Synchronization Reward for Audio-Visual Generation
Sound.summary: Recent years have witnessed rapid progress in joint audio--visual generation. However, audio--visual synchronization remains a challenge, as generated speech and sound often temporally misalign with visual events. A key bottleneck is the lack of human-annotated data, reliable evaluation benchmarks, and synchronization-aware evaluation models for generated audio--visual outputs. To address these limitations, we conduct a comprehensive study spanning data, benchmarking, and reward modeling. We first introduce SyncReward-Data-80K, a dataset containing 80K professional synchronization ratings for clips from eight audio--visual generators. A taxonomy-guided construction pipeline covers four sound-event families: Speech, Onset, Instrument, and Ambient. We further construct \textbf{SyncReward-Bench}, a held-out benchmark of 1K clips, each independently rated by multiple professionals. Using this benchmark, we systematically evaluate specialized synchronization metrics and omni-modal models, revealing their substantial misalignment with human judgments. Finally, we develop SyncReward, a reward model that combines semantic--temporal contrastive pretraining on real clips with human supervision on generated clips. As an evaluation metric, SyncReward achieves the strongest agreement with human ratings among the evaluated methods. As a reward, it improves synchronization through inference-time best-of-$N$ selection and reinforcement learning based post-training. We will release the data, benchmark, model, and code at https://github.com/WeChatCV/SyncReward.

Sound.title: What Matters in Preference Post-Training of Continuous Autoregressive Speech Language Models
Sound.summary: Continuous autoregressive speech language models combine an autoregressive (AR) backbone with a diffusion or flow-matching head. Preference post-training requires choosing how to construct pairs and which modules to update. Controlled interventions show that a perturbed acoustic patch changes subsequent backbone states, yet larger representation changes do not necessarily reduce speech quality. We construct preference pairs through noise or inference-configuration perturbations and formulate a preference update based on reference-relative flow-matching errors. Updating the backbone with a fixed head yields stronger reward improvements than head-only adaptation in our evaluated setting. Across flow-time and module ablations, the lowest training loss does not consistently produce the best speech. These findings support preference post-training that considers both acoustic sampling and autoregressive conditioning, with training choices validated on generated utterances.

Sound.title: FOAdapter: A Plug-and-Play Spatial Tokenizer for Low-Bitrate FOA Speech Coding
Sound.summary: Spatially encoded speech conveys not only linguistic information but also spatial cues. This enables listeners to distinguish and localize speakers, contributing to more natural and realistic auditory experiences in applications such as remote conferencing and immersive media. Neural speech codecs (NSCs) enable high-quality reconstruction of monaural speech at increasingly low bitrates while preserving linguistic information, but their ability to effectively preserve spatial cues remains limited. We propose FOAdapter, a plug-and-play spatial tokenizer that leverages a pretrained monaural speech codec to efficiently represent both linguistic and spatial information in first-order ambisonic (FOA) speech at low bitrates. Comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that FOAdapter consistently preserves spatial information across all evaluated codecs. Source code and audio examples are available on our demo website.

Sound.title: The NVVSpeech Challenge 2026: Overview and Lessons for Speech Understanding and Generation with Nonverbal Vocalizations
Sound.summary: Nonverbal vocalizations (NVVs), such as laughter and sighs, convey meaning alongside words. NVV-aware speech systems must recognize and generate these events while preserving lexical accuracy and perceptual quality. Yet differences in annotation, resources, and evaluation complicate comparisons, and aggregate scores can obscure specific weaknesses. We review ten system descriptions from the NVVSpeech Challenge 2026, covering understanding and generation in Chinese and English across 16 event categories. Our analysis examines supervision construction, task adaptation, and inference-time or preference-based feedback. Results reveal persistent recognition difficulties with breath and gasp and trade-offs between event recognition and lexical accuracy, as well as between generation intelligibility and acoustic quality, with human listening providing complementary evaluation evidence. These findings identify priorities for advancing NVV-aware speech understanding, controllable generation, and comparable evaluation.

Sound.title: Adaptive Compression and Targeted Perturbation: A Unified Framework for Generalized Audio Deepfake Detection
Sound.summary: Existing audio deepfake detection (ADD) methods frequently exhibit limited generalization, as fixed bottleneck architectures fail to adapt to the heterogeneous information densities inherent in diverse spoofing artifacts. Moreover, standard augmentation often leads to a pathological robustness-accuracy trade-off. In this paper, we propose a unified ADD framework to address these challenges. Our approach integrates: (1) an Adaptive Audio Feature Integration (AAFI) module that dynamically selects optimal latent dimensions via a compression pool and a stochastic exploration mechanism, ensuring flexible representations across multiple types of dynamic attacks; and (2) a Mel-Band Adversarial Perturbation (Mel-BAP) strategy that applies targeted regularization in the mel-spectrogram domain to encourage the model to learn invariant decision boundaries. Extensive evaluations on benchmarks including ADD 2022, FakeOrReal, and In-the-Wild demonstrate that our model based on Whisper-small achieves a state-of-the-art average Equal Error Rate (EER) of 1.51%. Compared to existing SOTA models such as the 3-billion-parameter Resemble-Detect-3B-Omni, our framework reduces the parameter count by up to 91.6% while achieving a 60.7% improvement in average EER. In a separate cross-lingual evaluation, the Whisper-base configuration achieves EERs of 3.91-5.65% on five unseen languages. The framework also maintains strong resilience to real-world acoustic distortions. This work provides a scalable and efficient "plug-in" solution for enhancing trust and security in the audio Web ecosystem.

Sound.title: Prime-EVC: One-Step Expressive Emotional Voice Conversion via Emotion-Primed Flow Matching
Sound.summary: Recent diffusion- and conditional flow matching (CFM)-based emotional voice conversion (EVC) systems achieve strong conversion quality. However, they typically rely on multiple sampling steps, because the conditioning specifies which emotion to impose while its acoustic realization is left to the sampler. In this paper, we propose Prime-EVC, a one-step expressive EVC architecture based on emotion-primed flow matching. Our key idea is to reallocate the emotional conversion between the conditioning and the sampler: a FiLM-fused speaker-emotion style, an emotional variance adaptor, and direct emotion and spectro-temporal supervision assemble an emotion-rich conditioning upstream, rendering the residual conversion left to the CFM decoder attainable within one Euler step. Experiments on the ESD corpus demonstrate that single-step Prime-EVC surpasses five representative EVC systems on every quality metric and exceeds 4- and 100-step DurFlex-EVC in subjective naturalness and emotion while running 3.4--50 times faster than both.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Co-Adaptive Entropy Modeling and Rate-Distortion-Optimal Bit Allocation for Perceptual Audio Coding
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: We present a perceptual audio coder in which the entropy-coding model and the bit allocation co-adapt across blocks without model side information. Mantissas are coded by a hybrid of bit packing and arithmetic coding with per-band probability models learned online. Encoder and decoder accumulate identical histograms from decoded blocks and advance the same model state. The model enters bit allocation directly: per-band rate--distortion frontiers combine measured perceptual distortion with entropy-coded rate estimates under the current model, and a dynamic program attains the exact minimum of total objective perceptual distortion for each block's budget under the model's rate estimates, with reservoir carry-over. Under a strict per-block rate, entropy-coding-aware bit allocation lowers this distortion (band noise-to-mask ratio in linear scale) by 15-24% relative to the same solver without it, and co-adaptation removes a further 3-4% (up to 15% on oboe) that a backward-adaptive coder alone cannot realize in one pass; a MUSHRA test at 80 kbps per channel confirms the ranking.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Active noise cancellation extends the benefit of AI speech enhancement in real hearing-aid recordings
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Active noise cancellation (ANC) is common in headphones but rare in hearing aids, and its value for understanding speech in noise is not established. Algorithms that improve signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) act only on the hearing aid's amplified path, while unprocessed sound also reaches the eardrum directly through the vent, limiting the SNR improvement that is realized. Our earlier simulations predicted that attenuating this direct path with ANC would substantially increase the benefit of such processing. We tested that prediction in three hardware conditions: a standard receiver-in-canal (RIC) hearing aid, and an ANC-capable RIC with ANC off and on. Each was fit to NAL-NL2 targets for an N3 hearing loss and recorded on KEMAR with an AI speech-enhancement algorithm (AI-SE) off and on, in seven realistic scenes above 70 dB SPL. Speech and noise spectra were estimated from each recording with a binary time-frequency mask derived from the clean speech. AI-SE produced a similar peak benefit of about 4 dB in the high frequencies in all three conditions, but that benefit stayed at or above 1 dB only above 1500, 600, and 130 Hz for the standard RIC, ANC RIC (ANC off), and ANC RIC (ANC on), respectively, closely tracking the measured attenuation of the direct path. With AI-SE on, ANC RIC (ANC on) improved SII-weighted SNR by 5.1 dB relative to the open ear, compared with 3.3 dB for ANC RIC (ANC off) and 1.6 dB for the standard RIC. With AI-SE off, enabling ANC added only 0.2 dB. ANC is therefore an enabling technology: on its own it added little, but by attenuating the direct path it allowed SNR-enhancing processing to deliver substantially greater benefit at the eardrum, extending that benefit to much lower frequencies.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: MSVAE: Rethinking Musical Semantics in Continuous Latent Spaces
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Continuous latent representations underlie recent diffusion-based lyrics-to-song and text-to-music systems, yet aligning lyric conditions with these latents remains difficult: existing systems resort to generator-side machinery such as sentence-level timestamps, auxiliary alignment objectives, or semi-autoregressive decoding, while the latents they predict are still produced by autoencoders trained purely for reconstruction. We address this difficulty from the representation side. We propose MSVAE (Music Semantic Variational Autoencoder), which structures its continuous latent around two complementary semantic streams: work-level compositional content and lyric-level linguistic-vocal content. Partitioned dual-stream alignment makes both streams explicit by aligning disjoint latent subspaces with frozen lead-sheet and ASR references, while a semantic-first gated residual posterior derives its base from a frozen music-SSL encoder and admits acoustic information only through gated, bounded corrections. MSVAE achieves competitive stereo reconstruction and stronger MARBLE probing than continuous-autoencoder baselines, and improves downstream lyrics-to-song and text-to-music generation. Notably, with only an untimed phoneme prefix and no lyric timing, MSVAE yields the lowest phoneme error rate, whereas all baseline representations require sentence-level alignment to produce intelligible vocals.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: SemBridge: Semantic Token Anchoring for Continuous-Latent Autoregressive Speech Generation
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Continuous-latent autoregressive speech generation has emerged as a promising alternative to discrete-token modeling by avoiding quantization loss and preserving richer acoustic information. However, continuous acoustic targets do not expose linguistic structure as explicit token-level prediction targets. Consequently, the autoregressive language model (LM) must acquire linguistic structure indirectly through acoustic prediction, which can compromise the content fidelity of generated speech. We propose SemBridge, a training-only semantic-token anchoring framework for continuous-latent autoregressive speech generation. SemBridge uses discrete semantic tokens to directly supervise autoregressive LM states and employs a Semantic-Aligned Acoustic VAE to organize the continuous target space under the same semantic reference. The semantic supervision is used only during training, while inference remains entirely continuous. We evaluate SemBridge on zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS) and score-conditioned singing voice synthesis (SVS). Across multiple benchmarks, SemBridge improves content accuracy, as measured by word and character error rates (WER/CER), while maintaining competitive speaker similarity and perceptual quality. Experimental results demonstrate that explicit semantic-token supervision for autoregressive state learning is an effective and general direction for continuous speech generation. The model code and checkpoints will be available at https://github.com/ASLP-lab/SemBridge

Audio and Speech Processing.title: SonicWorld: Source-Centric Latent Dynamics for Spatial Audio Reasoning
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Dynamic spatial audio reasoning requires a model to associate changing acoustic observations with the correct source and recover its spatial state at a queried time or interval, a challenge intensified by overlapping speech and source motion. To study this problem, we introduce Sonic-Bench, comprising 2.8K first-order Ambisonics clips and 28.8K target-specific question-answer pairs across 480 simulated indoor scenes. The benchmark covers localization, distance estimation, and motion reasoning in single- and dual-source settings. We further propose SonicWorld, which integrates physical, learned acoustic, and semantic features into persistent source states through learned transitions and recurrent updates, and projects them into an Omni LLM for spatial reasoning. Compared with Spatial-Omni on the Sonic-Bench test split, SonicWorld improves direction accuracy from 31.98% to 34.69% and reduces azimuth error from 57.22° to 48.01°. In zero-shot transfer to Spatial LibriSpeech, SonicWorld retains strong localization performance, achieving 73.98% direction accuracy and 19.29° azimuth error, compared with 27.14% and 70.74° for Spatial-Omni.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: D2: High-Capability Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models from Half-Duplex Backbones
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Full-duplex spoken language models (FD-SLMs) support simultaneous listening and speaking, but often lag behind half-duplex spoken language models (HD-SLMs) in general capabilities. We propose Dialogue-to-Duplex (D2), a framework that converts pretrained HD-SLMs into high-capability FD-SLMs at fine temporal granularity. D2 adapts the original audio encoder to streaming through decoder-free representation distillation and learns full-duplex interaction through supervised fine-tuning. We systematically study the effects of chunk size on full-duplex interaction, general capabilities, and inference computation. We apply D2 to two distinct HD-SLM architectures, Qwen3-Omni and LLaMA-Omni 2. At a 12.5Hz update rate, Qwen3-Omni-D2 achieves 99.2% turn-taking success with 521-ms latency, 99.5% interruption success, and a state-of-the-art VoiceBench score of 70.1.
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: 17 pages, including references and appendices. Demo: https://d2-duplex-demo.github.io/

Audio and Speech Processing.title: VocalCoachBench: Benchmarking Audio-Language Models on Expert Feedback for Singing
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Recent audio-language models are increasingly evaluated on recognizing, describing, and reasoning about audio, but expert-facing applications require a different capability: producing feedback that identifies problems and suggests corrective actions grounded in the input. We introduce VocalCoachBench, a benchmark for evaluating audio-language models on expert vocal coaching feedback for singing. VocalCoachBench contains 515 recordings annotated by 18 professional vocal trainers, yielding 1,056 expert submissions and 12,051 atomic coaching claims. It comprises a same-song subset for controlled comparison and a diverse-song subset for segment-grounded feedback across varied songs and recording conditions. To accommodate the open-ended nature of expert feedback, VocalCoachBench sep- arates deterministic structured targets from claim-based assessment of free-form diagnosis and corrective guidance. Human annotation analysis shows that expert agreement varies strongly with label granularity, motivating hierarchical structured metrics and claim-based evaluation of open-ended feedback. Experiments with 12 recent audio-language models reveal a consistent gap: while models can compare performances and identify broad issue domains in free-form feedback, Top-3 fine-grained issue-label identification remains below label-prior baselines and strict diagnosis alignment stays below 7%. To our knowledge, VocalCoachBench pro- vides the first public testbed for evaluating audio-grounded expert feedback for singing, moving audio-language evaluation beyond description toward analytic feedback.
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations & Datasets Track

Audio and Speech Processing.title: PitchIn: Natural-Language Vocal Coaching from Unstructured Community Feedback
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Effective vocal coaching connects performance issues with corrective advice, but recordings paired with expert diagnoses and advice are scarce. Online singing communities provide a potential source of supervision, but observations and advice are scattered across unstructured comments. We introduce PitchIn, audio-language models for natural-language vocal coaching, and the PeerCoach Dataset: 14,445 instruction examples covering Focused QA, Overall Feedback, and Recognition QA. We compare target combinations on Qwen2.5-Omni and train PitchIn on Focused QA and Overall Feedback using Qwen2.5-Omni and MOSS-Music. On VocalCoachBench, the proportion of requested diagnosis-correction pairs matching an expert issue with valid advice rises from 21.3% to 61.0% for Qwen2.5-Omni and from 31.4% to 51.2% for MOSS-Music. Direct training on source comments yields only 19.8% for Qwen2.5-Omni. For Qwen, Focused QA alone reaches 65.6%, but adding Overall Feedback improves alignment with expert reviews and human preference. Both models improve expert-review alignment over pretrained baselines and are significantly preferred for usefulness (92.0% and 67.3%, respectively). Demo examples are available at https://hayeonbang.github.io/PitchIn.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: StepAudio 3 Realtime Technical Report
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Realtime spoken interaction demands deep reasoning, prompt responses, and fluid turn-taking. We present StepAudio 3 Realtime, an audio-language foundation model organized around a continuous listen-converse-think-act loop. Deep Perception captures rich acoustic cues to interpret user intent, while Seamless Duplex models synchronized audio streams to handle pauses, backchannels, and interruptions naturally. Crucially, we resolve the tension between deep deliberation and latency via Think-While-Speaking, executing private reasoning in parallel with spoken delivery. In reasoning mode, StepAudio 3 reaches a 73.0 macro average on StepAudioChat. With Think-While-Speaking, it achieves dialogue and reasoning performance comparable to dedicated reasoning models while speaking in real time. Furthermore, an integrated Voice Agent handles asynchronous tool execution without disrupting the dialogue flow. StepAudio 3 Realtime achieves top-tier performance across key dimensions: an exceptional 90.6 on the MMSU benchmark, 98.9 Overall on the Artificial Analysis Full-Duplex Bench, and a 56.0% macro task-success rate on $τ$-Voice.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Spiking Neural Beamforming for Multichannel Speech Enhancement on the Edge
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Speech enhancement with wearable and edge devices requires architectures that balance enhancement quality against power and memory resources. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a promising path towards this goal through sparse, event-driven computation, but existing SNN-based speech enhancement methods are largely restricted to single-channel processing and therefore cannot exploit the spatial diversity available from microphone arrays. In this work, we propose a fully SNN framework for multichannel speech enhancement based on a fully connected architecture (FC-SNN) with sequential spike encoding, derived from a compact artificial neural network (ANN) baseline via leaky integrate-and-fire neurons. We characterize how enhancement performance scales with model size and spike-train length relative to ANN and classical beamforming baselines, and report the resulting parameter counts and computational complexity. We further compare direct and rate spike encoding, revealing a clear trade-off between event-driven computation and enhancement performance, and use these results to identify favorable configurations for edge devices.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Deep Speech Representations Track Word Timing along a Low-Dimensional Circular Trajectory
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Speech timing is fundamental for speech models to recognize words accurately, but how word-timing information is represented in speech models remains underexplored. We study this question using the framework of representational geometry, which investigates whether and how concepts are represented in low-dimensional subspaces of the representation space. Prior work in cognitive neuroscience has shown that when HuBERT feature sequences are averaged across words of the same duration, they form near-circular trajectories from word onset to word offset in a two-dimensional "temporal subspace." Here we show that this circular structure of word timing is a general property of deep speech representations, by demonstrating its emergence in nine additional speech models covering both supervised and self-supervised. We then move beyond averaged word segments and show that in HuBERT, the circular trajectories are consistent enough at the level of individual words to perform word segmentation. Our approach, Rotary Segmentation (RoSeg), achieves 64.3% boundary F-score on Librispeech by detecting word boundaries when cycles complete in the temporal subspace. Although supervision is needed to identify a good subspace, nevertheless this result demonstrates much stronger implicit word knowledge in HuBERT than has previously been shown.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation through Latent Subspace Coefficients Search
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Real-world deployment often exposes vision models to distribution shifts, making test-time adaptation (TTA) important for reliable prediction. Existing TTA methods can be difficult to deploy on edge devices because they require backpropagation, activation storage, or test-time batches, which increase computation, memory, and state. We propose \textbf{ELaTTA} (\textit{Efficient Latent Test-Time Adaptation}), a forward-only, gradient-free framework for single-instance TTA. ELaTTA freezes the pretrained model and adapts each test input by searching a low-dimensional coefficient vector in a principal latent subspace computed offline from a source-domain cache. The basis is stored once and source data are discarded before deployment. At test time, CMA-ES performs covariance-adaptive Gaussian search, ranks candidate corrections by prediction entropy, and selects the best candidate within a fixed evaluation budget. On five visual benchmarks spanning corruption, natural, rendition, sketch, and cross-domain shifts, ELaTTA provides strong accuracy under strict and continual single-instance protocols. In the strict single-instance comparison, MEMO requires \emph{64.7$\times$} the computation and \emph{12.4$\times$} the peak memory of ELaTTA. A complementary keyword-spotting experiment shows that the same coefficient-search design transfers beyond vision. We further demonstrate ViT-Base adaptation on a Raspberry Pi 5, confirming the feasibility of deploying ELaTTA on an edge device.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: RefTAG: Reflection-aware Temporal Audio Grounding in Large Audio Language Models
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Temporal audio grounding requires locating every occurrence of a queried target, making both occurrence counts and interval boundaries essential. We propose RefTAG, a post-training framework for verifiable temporal self-correction. Its Reflection Chain-of-Thought (Re-CoT) protocol combines draft intervals, discrete count and boundary actions, and revised intervals in one response. Supervised fine-tuning on these trajectories (Re-CoT-SFT) teaches the protocol; reinforcement learning (RL) jointly rewards final localization and revision outcomes. Across 8,228 queries, Re-CoT-SFT improves query-weighted mIoU over final-answer SFT by 1.74 percentage points. RL further improves TAG-Bench multi-target mIoU by 0.40 points and R@0.5 by 0.86 points. The final model achieves 38.50% TAG-Bench mIoU and 51.01% mean mIoU across three datasets, outperforming the evaluated open-source MOSS-Audio and FireRedAudio models and the commercial Gemini-3.1-Pro on both measures. These results demonstrate that explicitly coupling count- and boundary-aware revision with joint reward optimization provides an effective and verifiable path to temporal audio grounding.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: FOAdapter: A Plug-and-Play Spatial Tokenizer for Low-Bitrate FOA Speech Coding
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Spatially encoded speech conveys not only linguistic information but also spatial cues. This enables listeners to distinguish and localize speakers, contributing to more natural and realistic auditory experiences in applications such as remote conferencing and immersive media. Neural speech codecs (NSCs) enable high-quality reconstruction of monaural speech at increasingly low bitrates while preserving linguistic information, but their ability to effectively preserve spatial cues remains limited. We propose FOAdapter, a plug-and-play spatial tokenizer that leverages a pretrained monaural speech codec to efficiently represent both linguistic and spatial information in first-order ambisonic (FOA) speech at low bitrates. Comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that FOAdapter consistently preserves spatial information across all evaluated codecs. Source code and audio examples are available on our demo website.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Towards Privacy-Preserving ASR: Speaker-Level Machine Unlearning
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems are commonly designed to transcribe linguistic content independently of speaker identity. However, speaker-specific information can persist within the latent representations of ASR models, raising privacy concerns when training data includes sensitive individuals. While machine unlearning has been studied in several speech tasks, applying speaker unlearning to ASR remains challenging due to the strong entanglement of linguistic and speaker-related information in speech representations. In this work, we conduct a layer-wise analysis of Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) based ASR representations, revealing that speaker identity is primarily encoded in intermediate encoder layers. Based on this observation, we explore a feature-level unlearning strategy that targets these identity structures. Experiments on the VCTK corpus show that the proposed approach removes the influence of specific speakers while maintaining robust transcription performance.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Singlish, Can or Not? Fine-Tuning and Evaluating Zero-Shot TTS for Singapore English
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Zero-shot text-to-speech (ZS-TTS) achieves near-human quality for standard English, but it copies regional accents poorly. Prompted with a short Singlish utterance, state-of-the-art systems reproduce a speaker's timbre while flattening the accent toward generic English. We investigate whether targeted fine-tuning off-the-shelf ZS-TTS can close the gap for Singapore English (Singlish). We fine-tune two cutting-edge ZS-TTS models, Chatterbox and CosyVoice 3, on 50 Singlish speakers from the Infocomm Media Development Authority National Speech Corpus (IMDA NSC). Three speech distributions are evaluated: real recordings against off-the-shelf and fine-tuned generation driven by the same Singlish audio prompts. The evaluation covers four dimensions: naturalness, intelligibility, speaker similarity, and accent similarity. We separate adaptation (in-domain speakers seen during fine-tuning) from consistency (held-out speakers) to test whether accent transfer generalises beyond the training data. Fine-tuning raises accent similarity on in-domain and out-of-domain speakers for both Chatterbox and CosyVoice 3. It moves the generated distribution measurably toward real Singlish, with the gain persisting on held-out speakers. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of Singlish-accented TTS.
Audio and Speech Processing.comment: 7 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. Submitted to SLT 2026 IEEE

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Why Learning Rediscovers the Closed-Form Diagonal Regularizer
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: Recovering modal amplitudes from a few sensors requires regularization, and the shape of the penalty decides how strongly each mode is shrunk. The best shape depends on the truncation noise that discarded modes add to every measurement, which is unobserved and could be room-specific. We identify a diagonal saturation principle: for a single snapshot, isotropic truncation noise makes the Bayes-optimal Tikhonov shape a closed-form power law Gamma_k proportional to lambda_k^|s|, set by the prior alone and independent of the domain. The off-diagonal anisotropy equals the Herfindahl index H of the discarded-mode power exactly, Weyl's eigenvalue counting law fixes the number of discarded modes and hence H, and Berry's random-wave conjecture enters only through a diagonal term D, which we measure directly. Together they predict an approximately flat loss landscape over the penalty exponent, which leaves a learned diagonal regularizer little to gain from tuning the exponent per room. On simulated acoustic rooms the closed form stays within 5.83% of a per-room power-law oracle across observation windows, and three learned diagonal architectures track its error, the closest within a fraction of a point and none more than 3pp above it, while learning qualitatively different spectra. In the truncation regime no tested method consistently improves on the closed form, including Learned Iterative Ridge, which couples modes across layers. The framework extends to heat diffusion through a known Green's-function correction with no new free parameters.

Audio and Speech Processing.title: Personal VAD: Speaker-Conditioned Voice Activity Detection
Audio and Speech Processing.summary: In this paper, we propose "personal VAD", a system to detect the voice activity of a target speaker at the frame level. This system is useful for gating the inputs to a streaming on-device speech recognition system, such that it only triggers for the target user, which helps reduce the computational cost and battery consumption, especially in scenarios where a keyword detector is unpreferable. We achieve this by training a VAD-alike neural network that is conditioned on the target speaker embedding or the speaker verification score. For each frame, personal VAD outputs the probabilities for three classes: non-speech, target speaker speech, and non-target speaker speech. Under our optimal setup, we are able to train a model with only 130K parameters that outperforms a baseline system where individually trained standard VAD and speaker recognition networks are combined to perform the same task.

Sound.title: NaijaS2ST: A Multi-Accent Benchmark for Speech-to-Speech Translation in Low-Resource Nigerian Languages
Sound.summary: Speech translation for low-resource languages remains fundamentally limited by the scarcity of high-quality, diverse parallel speech data, a challenge that is especially pronounced in African linguistic contexts. To address this, we introduce NaijaS2ST, a parallel speech translation dataset spanning Igbo, Hausa, Yorùbá, and Nigerian Pidgin paired with English. The dataset comprises approximately 50 hours of speech per language and captures substantial variation in speakers and accents, reflecting realistic multilingual and multi-accent conditions. With NaijaS2ST, we conduct a comprehensive benchmark of cascaded, end-to-end (E2E), and AudioLLM-based approaches across bidirectional translation settings. Our results show that audio LLMs with few-shot examples are more effective for speech-to-text translation than cascaded and end-to-end methods trained on fine-tuned data. However, for speech-to-speech translation, the cascaded and audio LLM paradigms yield comparable performance, indicating that there is still considerable room for improvement in developing targeted, task-specific models for this setting. By providing both a high-quality dataset and a systematic benchmark, we hope that NaijaS2ST will serve as a strong foundation for advancing research in low-resource, multilingual speech translation.

Sound.title: TASTE: Taxonomy-Aware Symbolic Piano Generation from Textual Description
Sound.summary: Text-conditioned symbolic music generation has attracted growing interest with the development of generative models. Yet two questions remain underexplored: what aspects of music the conditioning text should describe, and how the corresponding data should be collected and trained to improve controllability and text-music alignment. We address these challenges with TASTE, a taxonomy-aware framework for symbolic music generation with a main focus on piano pieces. First, we introduce a taxonomy of musical elements that specifies how a piece can be captured through textual description in a musically grounded way. The taxonomy comprises a set of metadata tags (genre, emotion, section plan, etc.) together with a free-form description of music imagery. This structure decomposes textual input to match the generation goal more coherently and precisely. Second, we build a data pipeline for collecting, annotating, and retrieving public symbolic piano resources, yielding a corpus of 432K MIDI files labeled at multiple levels of granularity. Finally, we design a staged training procedure that leverages this multi-granularity data across two model families: an autoregressive model and a non-autoregressive diffusion model. Both objective and subjective evaluations show that our models achieve superior musical-element control, text-description alignment, and overall music quality. We will release the full pipeline, all annotated datasets, and the model checkpoints.

Sound.title: Harmonic Representations in Symbolic Music Transformers are Localized and Controllable
Sound.summary: Transformer models trained on symbolic music have become remarkably capable. However, it is yet unclear how they represent music structure, and whether understanding their internal representations can be used to unlock methods for model control. We examine this through a case study of harmonic analysis: when a music transformer navigates a cadence, what does it internally "know" about its harmonic context, and can that knowledge be used to affect the generation? Using Aria, a LLaMA-based symbolic music transformer evaluated on Bach chorales, we find that harmonic decisions are causally localized progressively from middle layers onward. Linear probes show that mode becomes decodable in the same layer range where patching identifies growing causal effect, while key identity emerges later. We then confirm these representations are actionable for music generation control: steering via latent directions corresponding to harmonic changes reliably produces a deceptive or minor resolution, while preserving structural coherence and generation quality. This demonstrates that, at inference time, the model's internal harmonic knowledge can be directly manipulated to control the harmonic output.
Sound.comment: 9 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. Accepted at ISMIR 2026 (27th International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference)

Sound.title: Listen, Reason, and Segment: Aligning LALMs with Editorial Judgment for Media Chapterization
Sound.summary: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) have made rapid progress on standardized benchmarks, yet their deployment in practical media workflows, curation, archival indexing, and content distribution remains largely unrealized. We identify automated audio chapterization, the task of segmenting continuous audio streams into thematically coherent chapters, as a demanding and commercially consequential setting that exposes this gap. Chapterization is challenging because boundaries are defined less by objective acoustic events than by subjective editorial judgment, requiring models to reason sequentially over long acoustic contexts and approximate creator-authored boundary decisions. We present AudioChaps, a post-training framework for aligning end-to-end LALMs for this task via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) guided by Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. To support training and evaluation, we curate three datasets: AudioChaps-Alignment, derived from creator-annotated chapter boundaries on YouTube; AudioChaps-CoT, which provides structured supervision for well-formatted, high-quality, and evidence-grounded boundary reasoning; and AudioChaps-Eval, a held-out benchmark for audio chapterization. Applying GRPO directly without a Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) cold start, AudioChaps-R1-Zero already improves average F1 by 33 points over the state-of-the-art LALM Audio-Flamingo-3-Think. The AudioChaps framework produces our final aligned LALM, AudioChaps-R1, which improves average F1 by 49 points. These results demonstrate that GRPO-trained LALMs can reliably transform unstructured auditory streams into navigable, structured media. Our code, models, and dataset resources will be released upon acceptance at https://github.com/ta012/AudioChaps.

Sound.title: A Situational Speech Synthesizer for Yoruba: System Design, Phonological Rule Architecture, and Orthographic Extensions for Contour
Sound.summary:
We present TTSYoruba, a rule-based concatenative diphone speech synthesizer for Yoruba, deployed at online as part of the YorubaName.com open dictionary of Yoruba personal names. The system takes tone-marked Yoruba text as input and produces audio output by applying a hand-crafted phonological rule system to a recorded inventory of 651 diphone units spanning five tonal variants of every consonant-vowel combination in the language. We describe the phonological architecture of the system in detail, including our complete tonal file-selection logic, our treatment of the three-way nasal disambiguation problem (oral /n/, nasalized vowel, and syllabic nasal), and the derivation of contextual rising and falling tones from level-tone input. We also present, as an orthographic contribution, the adoption of the caron and circumflex, which are symbols with prior standing in Yoruba phonological transcription, as standard single-vowel contour tone markers, integrated into the TTS normalization pipeline and the WriteYoruba keyboard input tool. The system's performance was evaluated through a listener study (N=50), with detailed results on Mean Opinion Scores (MOS) presented in Section 6.
  Keywords: Yoruba, text-to-speech, low-resource languages, diphone synthesis, contour tones, African language NLP, rule-based synthesis
Sound.comment: 18 pages. v4: updated citations to the companion paper (arXiv:2609.38627), which proposes the caron/circumflex convention as a revision of the standard Yoruba orthography; corrected rulebook entry numbers and the Adenike example in Section 5 to match the deposited rule specification; fixed missing characters (equivalence symbol, IPA and syllabic-nasal marks); improved table layout

Sound.title: FlowGRPO for Vocal Separation: From Reward Analysis to Reward Design
Sound.summary: The Flow Matching objective supervises the velocity field at intermediate states, whereas waveform metrics are evaluated after decoding and may be non-differentiable. To align Flow Matching models with waveform-level and perceptual quality objectives during post-training, FlowGRPO optimizes their trajectories using endpoint rewards. In this work, we focus on music separation and use multi-resolution short-time Fourier transform (MRSTFT), scale-invariant signal-to-distortion ratio (SI-SDR), and Virtual Speech Quality Objective Listener (ViSQOL) as reward components. Before policy optimization, we analyze the relationship between data quality factors and the within-group gap between the maximum and mean rollout rewards for each component. This analysis motivates a revised ViSQOL reward that matches channel-wise root-mean-square (RMS) levels and evaluates the interval from the first to the last active frame, retaining inactive frames within that interval. We also apply a sample-quality filter based on predefined waveform checks. Together, the revised reward and quality filter enable FlowGRPO to improve the pretrained vocal separator in both separation performance and perceptual quality.

Sound.title: CodecFlow: Efficient Bandwidth Extension via Conditional Flow Matching in Neural Codec Latent Space
Sound.summary: Speech Bandwidth Extension improves clarity and intelligibility by restoring/inferring appropriate high-frequency content for low-bandwidth speech. Existing methods often rely on spectrogram or waveform modeling, which can incur higher computational cost and have limited high-frequency fidelity. Neural audio codecs offer compact latent representations that better preserve acoustic detail, yet accurately recovering high-resolution latent information remains challenging due to representation mismatch. We present CodecFlow, a neural codec-based BWE framework that performs efficient speech reconstruction in a compact latent space. CodecFlow employs a voicing-aware conditional flow converter on continuous codec embeddings and a structure-constrained residual vector quantizer to improve latent alignment stability. Optimized end-to-end, CodecFlow achieves strong spectral fidelity and enhanced perceptual quality on 8 kHz to 16 kHz and 44.1 kHz speech BWE tasks.

Sound.title: Synthesizing Ultrasonic Echo Profiles from Text for Open-Vocabulary Silent Speech Recognition
Sound.summary: Eyewear that senses articulation with inaudible ultrasound can now recognize silent speech over an open vocabulary, but its accuracy is limited by the cost of training data. We present SoniGAN, which synthesizes the ultrasonic echo profiles of silent articulation from text and uses them as synthetic supervision. A voice-cloned text-to-speech (TTS) model reads a text corpus, and a two-stage generator synthesizes echo profiles from representations of the spoken content of that audio. Pretraining a recognizer on 104 hours of the synthesized data improves the word error rate (WER) of a public open-vocabulary benchmark by 2.3 points. Adding the sessions the corpus discards for a faulty microphone brings the system to 22.2% without any language model. Lexicon-constrained decoding, LLM rescoring, and ensembling further bring it to 14.9%, the first minimally obtrusive silent speech interface to fall inside the error range in which users report no loss of willingness to use silent speech input.

Sound.title: AnyEdit: A Unified Framework for Speech and Singing Voice Editing with Real-World Environmental Consistency
Sound.summary: We present AnyEdit, a unified, separation-free framework for speech and singing voice editing that preserves real-world acoustic environments, including noise, reverberation, and background music. Recent unified generative models already achieve strong speech and singing generation in clean conditions, but real-world vocal editing remains challenging because the model must revise content while simultaneously preserving speaker identity, prosody, and the surrounding acoustic scene. Directly modeling noisy audio end-to-end entangles semantic editing with environmental acoustics, weakening the core vocal generation capability. We therefore adopt a two-stage design that preserves clean-domain editing ability while deferring acoustic rendering to a separate stage: an instruction-guided autoregressive editor first predicts clean prosody and content-style tokens, supported by a teacher-student noise-robust prosody tokenizer that distills clean prosodic tokens from degraded recordings; a flow-matching acoustic model then performs in-context rendering conditioned on the source acoustic context, so the edited segment inherits surrounding noise, reverberation, and background sound while maintaining consistent speaker timbre. To stabilize unedited regions, we introduce unmodified-area-aware supervision; after pre-training, we further apply direct preference optimization on mined real-to-real singing pairs. We also release AnyEditBench, a benchmark covering both speech and singing voice editing under clean, simulated, and in-the-wild acoustic conditions. Experiments on Chinese and English speech and singing datasets showed that AnyEdit consistently outperforms strong baselines in content accuracy, subjective quality, and background consistency under noisy and reverberant conditions. Demo: https://any-edit.github.io/. AnyEditBench: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Ririiiii/anyeditbench.

Sound.title: Fast Diffusion-GAN Model for Generating Symbolic Music with Emotions
Sound.summary: Diffusion models have shown promising results for a wide range of generative tasks with continuous data, such as image and audio synthesis. However, little progress has been made on using diffusion models to generate symbolic music since this class of generative models struggles with discrete data while its iterative sampling process is computationally expensive. In this work, we propose a diffusion model integrated with a Generative Adversarial Network, aiming to mitigate the slow sampling drawback of diffusion models applied to symbolic music generation. We enable the use of diffusion model by representing symbolic music as image-like pianorolls with velocity values instead of discrete event tokens and then used a Variational Autoencoder to obtain their latent representations to train the proposed diffusion model. Our results demonstrate the successful control of our diffusion model to generate symbolic music with a desired emotion. Our model uses merely 15 denoising diffusion steps to produce high-quality music, while most diffusion models for symbolic music generation require hundreds or thousands of steps.

Sound.title: Sleep Sound Event Detection Powered by Learnable Multi-Resolution Adaptive Line Enhancer
Sound.summary: Sleep-disordered breathing, including snoring, hypopnea, and obstructive apnea, is the hallmark of obstructive sleep apnea, whose severity is quantified by the Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI). As conventional polysomnography is costly and clin- ically demanding, microphone-only detection has emerged as a noninvasive alternative for screening. We propose ALE- Confidence Fusion Sound Event Detection (ACF-SED), the first framework that directly injects the per-frame confidence map of an Adaptive Line Enhancer (ALE) into Transformer atten- tion biasing and feature modulation, rather than as mere pre- processing. A Multi-Resolution ALE Bank aggregates three parallel NLMS filters at distinct decorrelation delays, while a Confidence-Guided Cross-Path block couples event and noise streams via gated cross-attention. On the Audio-Polygraphy Dataset for Sleep Apnea Analysis, ACF-SED achieves state- of-the-art detection across Event-F1, Segment-F1, and PSDS, enabling end-to-end AHI estimation.

Sound.title: Sori: Streamable and Controllable Model for Non-musical Audio to Symbolic Music Transformation
Sound.summary: We introduce Non-musical Audio to Symbolic Music Transformation (NASMT), a novel task that converts non-musical audio into symbolic music representations. Unlike automatic music transcription, which assumes musical input and a unique correct score, NASMT is inherently one-to-many and requires evaluation along two axes: input correspondence and musicality. We present Sori, an encoder--decoder Transformer that addresses this task through domain adversarial training (DAT), which bridges the gap between musical and non-musical audio in the encoder's feature space, and classifier-free guidance (CFG) with a continuous parameter~$γ$ that controls the trade-off between correspondence and musicality at inference time. Across objective metrics and a listening study, Sori provides effective continuous control via $γ$ and compares favorably with instrument-agnostic transcription models. Sori supports real-time streaming on a consumer CPU. Audio examples are available at https://soridemo0320.github.io/sori-demo/.

Sound.title: Generating Synthetic Doctor-Patient Conversations for Long-form Audio Summarization
Sound.summary: Long-context audio reasoning is underserved in both training data and evaluation. Existing benchmarks target short-context tasks, and the open-ended generation tasks most relevant to long-context reasoning pose well-known challenges for automatic evaluation. We propose a synthetic data generation pipeline designed to serve both as a training resource and as a controlled evaluation environment, and instantiate it for first-visit doctor-patient conversations with SOAP note generation as the task. The pipeline has three stages, persona-driven dialogue generation, multi-speaker audio synthesis with overlap/pause modeling, room acoustics, and sound events, and LLM-based reference SOAP note production, built entirely on open-weight models. We release 8,800 synthetic conversations with 1.3k hours of corresponding audio and reference notes. Evaluating current open-weight systems, we find that cascaded approaches still substantially outperform end-to-end models.
Sound.comment: Published at Interspeech 2026. v2 is the published version; results were corrected after a bug fix: end-to-end and cascaded systems now perform comparably (per-claim hallucination 32% vs. 22-24%)

Sound.title: BridgeCodec: Mamba Enhanced Neural Audio Codec with Schrödinger Bridge at Low Bitrate
Sound.summary: Neural audio codecs achieve remarkable performance but operate as closed ecosystems with rigidly co-trained encoderdecoder pairs, severely hindering interoperability. To resolve this, we propose BridgeCodec, a versatile framework that decouples these pairs by translating latent representations between mismatched, frozen endpoints. We formulate this cross-codec translation as a Schrödinger Bridge optimal transport problem, enabling robust mapping between disparate distributions without predefined noise priors. To efficiently capture longrange speech temporal dependencies, we integrate a Mambaenhanced U-Net architecture. We validate BridgeCodec on an extreme deployment scenario: mapping a lightweight 8 kHz source encoder directly to a 48 kHz target decoder at an ultralow bitrate of 1 kbps. Experimental results demonstrate that BridgeCodec achieves superior wideband reconstruction and high perceptual quality, successfully bridging heavily bottlenecked, heterogeneous codecs.

Sound.title: Learning from Real Stuttering: Synthetic Mandarin Stuttering Speech for Data Augmentation in Speech Recognition
Sound.summary: Mandarin stuttered speech remains under-resourced, limiting the development of robust speech processing systems. We present a Mandarin stuttering speech synthesis and data augmentation framework that adapts both autoregressive and non-autoregressive TTS models using naturally stuttered speech. Specifically, we adapt CosyVoice2 and MaskGCT to support controllable generation of specific stuttering events while also modeling broader utterance-level characteristics of stuttered speech. Using the adapted models, we construct synthetic data resources for downstream augmentation. Evaluations show that the generated speech closely approaches real stuttered speech. Extensive ASR experiments demonstrate consistent augmentation gains and further observe a domain-gap--diversity trade-off between synthetic and real data. These results demonstrate the value of learning synthetic stuttering data directly from real dysfluency for robust Mandarin speech processing.

Sound.title: PhyAVBench: A Challenging Audio Physics-Sensitivity Benchmark for Physically Grounded Text-to-Audio-Video Generation
Sound.summary: Text-to-audio-video (T2AV) generation is central to applications such as filmmaking and world modeling. However, current models often fail to produce physically plausible sounds. Previous benchmarks primarily focus on audio-video temporal synchronization, while largely overlooking explicit evaluation of audio-physics grounding, thereby limiting the study of physically plausible audio-visual generation. To address this issue, we present PhyAVBench, the first benchmark that systematically evaluates the audio-physics grounding capabilities of T2AV, image-to-audio-video (I2AV), and video-to-audio (V2A) models. PhyAVBench offers PhyAV-Sound-11K, a new dataset of 25.5 hours of 11,605 audible videos collected from 184 participants to ensure diversity and avoid data leakage. It contains 337 paired-prompt groups with controlled physical variations that drive sound differences, each grounded with an average of 17 videos and spanning 6 audio-physics dimensions and 41 fine-grained test points. Each prompt pair is annotated with the physical factors underlying their acoustic differences. Importantly, PhyAVBench leverages paired text prompts to evaluate this capability. We term this evaluation paradigm the Audio-Physics Sensitivity Test (APST) and introduce a novel metric, the Contrastive Physical Response Score (CPRS), which quantifies the acoustic consistency between generated videos and their real-world counterparts. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of 17 state-of-the-art models. Our results reveal that even leading commercial models struggle with fundamental audio-physical phenomena, exposing a critical gap beyond audio-visual synchronization and pointing to future research directions. We hope PhyAVBench will serve as a foundation for advancing physically grounded audio-visual generation. Prompts, ground-truth, and generated video samples are available at https://github.com/imxtx/PhyAVBench.
Sound.comment: 6 major physical dimensions, 41 fine-grained test points, 337 groups of variable-controlled test samples, 11,605 newly recorded videos

Sound.title: LiveAnon: Improving Privacy and Utility in Streaming Speaker Anonymization with Codec Language Models
Sound.summary: Speaker anonymization (SA) aims to conceal speaker identity while preserving linguistic content and emotion, but existing streaming systems often lose emotion information through discrete content bottlenecks or require emotion-specific modeling. We present LiveAnon, a voice-conversion-based streaming SA system that directly conditions an autoregressive codec language model on hidden features from a pretrained streaming ASR encoder, preserving emotion without emotion-specific supervision. To reduce codec-generation latency, we introduce capped RVQ decoding, which preserves dependencies among coarse codebooks while predicting the remaining codebooks in parallel. Under VPC24, LiveAnon improves intelligibility and emotion preservation over fixed-target Stream-Voice-Anon (SVA), a strong prior streaming SA system, matches emotion-prompted SVA in emotion preservation, and achieves the strongest semi-informed privacy among streaming systems. Under VPC26, it ranks second across all metrics among the evaluated anonymization systems, demonstrating a strong privacy-utility balance.

Sound.title: JSIR: An Audio-Aligned, Multi-Task Dataset of Jazz Standard Recordings
Sound.summary: Beat tracking, chord estimation, and structure analysis are staple tasks of music information retrieval. Their datasets are drawn largely from Western popular music, and jazz remains a repertoire on which state-of-the-art systems underperform. We present JSIR, the Jazz Standards dataset for Information Retrieval. Its 267 recordings of 44 jazz standards span 25.6 hours, 3.7 times the audio of JAAH, the closest existing resource. For each recording, we provide annotations for beat and downbeat positions, chords, and sections, all produced by a jazz musician and revised in several passes. In baseline experiments, models trained with JSIR also improve on other jazz datasets: the downbeat F-measure of a state-of-the-art beat tracker rises from 87.7% to 89.2%, and the seventh-chord accuracy of a pop-trained chord estimator on JAAH from 34% to 41%. We publicly release the annotations, the annotation tool used to create them, and a web application that displays them in sync with the audio.
Sound.comment: Submitted to IEEE ICASSP 2027; 5 pages, 1 figure

Sound.title: Gugak-VocalSet: A Multi-Genre Studio-Quality Dataset of Korean Traditional Singing with Sigimsae Annotations
Sound.summary: We present Gugak-VocalSet, the first publicly available audio dataset for Korean traditional singing with dense annotations of sigimsae, a structured pitch contour system of vocal expressions. Gugak-VocalSet contains 24.5 hours of unaccompanied solo vocal recordings across 305 tracks of representative repertoire curated by the National Gugak Center, performed by 20 professional singers in a controlled studio environment with fixed key and tempo. In addition to genre, lyrics, and mood/timbre tags, the dataset provides a unified sigimsae ontology and approximately 68,000 segments (71,700 instances including multi-label) of audio-grounded sigimsae annotations; the ontology adopts a functional-position-based hierarchy designed for consistent application across genres, and 14 expert annotators specializing in Korean traditional music performed segment-level labeling accordingly. Baseline experiments on sigimsae classification and event detection show that domain-informed F0 representations remain competitive with, and on classification surpass, frozen probing of a general-purpose music foundation model, while pitch and spectral cues play complementary roles in event-level detection. Companion page: https://www.danbinaerin.com/Gugak-VocalSet/
